verdict_explanation: No paper occupies the EXACT conjunction (code-generation LLM expresses its OWN calibrated, discriminative confidence at per-test-case/per-requirement granularity, execution-verified, evaluated by localization/discrimination AUROC). That precise cell is confirmed empty by both the vault's full-text locus investigation and fresh adversarial arXiv/Semantic Scholar search (DCPO's own citation graph, 4 papers, contains no structured-code-confidence follow-up). HOWEVER, three adjacent literatures are dense enough that the novelty claim is fragile if the draft frames it as 'nobody has decomposed code confidence into fine-grained units': (1) code fault-localization / line-level diagnostic-uncertainty papers for REPAIR (FLARE, faulty-token-localization work) already predict WHICH region of code will fail and use execution outcomes to validate/select, just via a separate diagnostic model and refinement-accuracy metrics, not expressed self-confidence + calibration/AUROC; (2) general-LLM claim-level/atomic confidence decomposition + RL calibration (Atomic Calibration of LLMs, CURE/'Think Through Uncertainty') already establishes 'decompose the response into verifiable sub-units and calibrate each with RL' as a 2024-2026 paradigm outside code -- a reviewer can construct 'CURE/Atomic-Calibration but for code, where test cases replace atomic claims' as an obvious-combination critique; (3) VeRPO already exploits per-test-case partial-success as free dense supervision for RL in code generation (for the correctness reward, not confidence), undercutting the claim that per-test labels are an unexploited resource. The draft's central task is not to prove non-existence in the abstract, but to make the execution-verifiability + expressed-interface + discrimination-metric conjunction explicitly load-bearing against all three adjacent literatures, not just against DCPO.

closest_papers.title: FLARE: Fine-Grained Diagnostic Feedback for LLM Code Refinement
closest_papers.what_it_does: A lightweight diagnostic model predicts LINE-LEVEL suspiciousness signals for bug localization; Flare searches top-k suspicious regions and selects the best candidate by execution outcome, improving iterative code refinement on LiveCodeBench/BigCodeBench across 5 base LLMs (1.7-8.5pp absolute gains).
closest_papers.why: Closest hit found in the entire search: it does localize WHICH part of code is likely wrong using execution feedback. But (a) the diagnostic signal comes from a SEPARATE lightweight model, not the code-generating LLM's own expressed output -- same category problem RLCM's probe has; (b) granularity is per-LINE (bug suspicion for repair), not per-TEST-CASE/per-requirement; (c) primary metric is downstream refinement pass-rate improvement, not calibration/discrimination (ECE/AUROC) of the localization signal itself -- abstract gives no AUROC/ECE number. Full text unread; MUST be fetched and explicitly distinguished in related work before the headline locks.

closest_papers.title: Think Through Uncertainty: Improving Long-Form Generation Factuality via Reasoning Calibration (CURE)
closest_papers.what_it_does: General-LLM long-form generation: explicitly critiques 'existing approaches remain limited to a single scalar confidence for the entire response, which is insufficient... where uncertainty varies across individual claims,' and proposes an RL framework (CURE) that estimates confidence per-claim, incorporating calibration into the RL objective for long-form factuality.
closest_papers.why: This is the closest METHODOLOGICAL analog outside code: decompose a response into verifiable sub-units and RL-train per-unit calibrated confidence, using exactly the 'single scalar is insufficient' argument the target paper's headline relies on. Domain-distinct (QA/factuality claims, not code) and label source differs (LLM-judged claim veracity, not free execution-verified per-test outcomes) -- the code-execution-verifiability of ground truth is the genuine structural difference and must be made explicit and load-bearing, not left implicit. Full text unread; fetch to extract exact RL/loss design so the draft's method section can cite and differentiate precisely.

closest_papers.title: Atomic Calibration of LLMs in Long-Form Generations
closest_papers.what_it_does: Decomposes long-form LLM responses into atomic claims and studies fine-grained (atomic) factuality calibration per claim, vs. prior single response-level (macro) calibration; proposes confidence-fusion strategies.
closest_papers.why: Establishes that 'decompose into fine-grained verifiable units + calibrate each unit' is an existing (2024) general-LLM paradigm, not a novel idea in the abstract. Pre-empts the paper claiming general novelty for the DECOMPOSITION IDEA itself; the paper's novelty must rest specifically on code's execution-verifiable, hallucination-free per-test ground truth as the differentiator from claim-level (LLM-judged) decomposition, and on training the GENERATING model's own expressed output (not a separate scorer).

closest_papers.title: Fine-grained Approaches for Confidence Calibration of LLMs in Automated Code Revision
closest_papers.what_it_does: Already fully read in-vault (locus code-verbal-calibration-occupied-or-open). Fine-grained (non-sequence-level) confidence scores for code REVISION across 14 models; internal/logit-derived signals only (min-token-prob, lowest-K, attention-weighted), post-hoc Platt scaling, discrimination via Kendall tau_b/Wasserstein-1, not AUROC.
closest_papers.why: Confirmed DISTINCT on three axes (code revision not generation; internal/logit not verbalized/expressed; tau_b/W1 not AUROC) but it is the nearest-neighbor CODE-domain paper using the word 'fine-grained' for calibration, and its own text explicitly flags the discrimination-collapse risk this proposal is designed around ('this type of degenerate confidence score...cannot support decision-making or thresholding'). Must be cited as the field's closest existing attempt and distinguished point-by-point in the draft; no new fetch needed, already at full-text depth.

closest_papers.title: Beyond Binary: Turning Partial Success into Dense Verifiable Rewards for RL in Code Generation (VeRPO)
closest_papers.what_it_does: Uses per-TEST-CASE partial success (passing a subset of tests) as an intrinsic, verifiable dense reward signal for RL training of code-generation CORRECTNESS; identifies and corrects a cardinality bias where policy updates over-favor easy-test gains.
closest_papers.why: Different target entirely (accuracy/correctness reward, not confidence/calibration) so it does not occupy the headline cell. But it independently confirms that per-test-case outcomes are a recognized, already-exploited free signal in code RL -- weakening (not killing) the framing that these labels are an unexploited resource, and its cardinality-bias finding (easy vs. hard test imbalance corrupting the reward) is a direct methodological risk transfer candidate for a per-test CONFIDENCE objective, which will also see imbalanced per-test difficulty. Should be cited as adjacent precedent and its bias analysis checked against the proposed training recipe.
